task.title: Lunar Combustion Investigation: Flammability Results from a Rotating Sounding Rocket

original_pages.text:
Schematic
Centrifugal gravity is into the page; this 
would be looking outward from the 
axis of rotation of the vehicle toward 
the cylindrical hull of the rocket.  The 
flames would generally rise out of the 
page, or towards the axis of rotation.
Two samples: Fabric 5 cm wide x 30 cm 
long and 4-mm-DIA acrylic, (PMMA); 
ignited with slight pause between 
them.

concentration, pressure, temperature,

The LUCI project achieved the first-ever, extended duration combustion tests (greater than 25 seconds) in simulated 
Lunar gravity.  The results are applicable to NASA’s exploration efforts in that they guide the selection of fire-safe 
materials and environments and ensure safety of future spacecraft and Lunar habitats.  The data also provides 
fundamental understanding of fires burning at reduced gravity for comparison to sophisticated numerical models.  
Finally, the experiment is a steppingstone to the ultimate goal of performing burn tests on the Lunar surface in the 
Flammability of Materials on the Moon (FM2) experiment which will fly on a SpaceX Human Lander System 
unmanned test flight.

Interpret only supplied original NASA evidence. Return JSON with keys
entities, quantities, statements. Each is an array of objects. Entities: label,
kind, page, quote. Quantities: label, expression, unit, subject, epistemic, page,
quote. Statements: text, subject, epistemic, page, quote. Every quote must be an
exact contiguous original span. Preserve approximate values, original units,
scope and uncertainty. Separate experimental_configuration, reported_quantity,
derived_quantity, measured_observation, author_conclusion, tentative_interpretation,
planned_work. A linear fit is derived, not a direct measurement. Do not infer
causes, executed runs, or distribute group results to other groups. Recover all
scientifically meaningful content, omit diagram-symbol fragments.
